title: Library of Congress Sound Recording and Film Preservation Programs Reauthorization Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on July 13, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Library of Congress Sound Recording and Film Preservation Programs Reauthorization Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the National Recording Preservation Act of 2000 to reauthorize through FY2026 the national sound recording preservation program of the Library of Congress and the National Recording Preservation Foundation in an amount not to exceed the lesser of $1 million or (as under current law) the amount of private contributions whether in currency, services, or property made to the Foundation by private persons and state and local governments.

The number of members of the Board of Directors of the National Recording Preservation Foundation shall be increased from 9 to 12, at least 8 of whom (currently, at least 6) must be knowledgeable or experienced in sound recording production, distribution, preservation, or restoration.

(Sec. 3) The bill amends the National Film Preservation Act of 1996 to reauthorize through FY2026 the National Film Registry of the Library of Congress and the National Film Preservation Foundation.

summary.headline: A law that extends federal programs for preserving sound recordings and films through 2026 and changes the size and makeup of one foundation's board.
summary.what_it_does: It extends the Library of Congress's national sound recording preservation program and the National Recording Preservation Foundation through fiscal year 2026, with funding capped at the lesser of $1 million or the private contributions the Foundation receives. It increases the Foundation's board from 9 to 12 members and requires at least 8 of them to have knowledge or experience in sound recording work. It also extends the National Film Registry and the National Film Preservation Foundation through fiscal year 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Library of Congress and its sound recording preservation program
who_it_affects.how: The program's authorization is extended through fiscal year 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the National Recording Preservation Foundation's board of directors
who_it_affects.how: The board grows from 9 seats to 12, with at least 8 members needing sound recording experience.

who_it_affects.group: Private donors and state and local governments that contribute to the National Recording Preservation Foundation
who_it_affects.how: Their contributions set the ceiling on federal funding, which is the lesser of $1 million or the amount they give.

who_it_affects.group: Film archivists and the National Film Preservation Foundation
who_it_affects.how: The National Film Registry and the Foundation are reauthorized through fiscal year 2026.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The reauthorizations run through fiscal year 2026; the bill summary does not give a specific start date.
